newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks close mixed, resist Wall St fall.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks close mixed, resist Wall St fall.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks ended mixed in light dealings, helped by stronger golds despite weakness in most sectors.
* Market depressed by Wall Street's extended sell-off.
Toronto stocks ended mixed in thin dealings on Monday, resisting New York's continued sell-off with the help of stronger key gold issues.
"Stocks didn't do too badly today, thanks to strength in the gold sector," said ScotiaMcLeod's senior vice-president Fred Ketchen.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index rose 7.18 points to 6040.76 in turnover of 87 million shares worth C$1.29 billion.
But declining issues beat out advancing ones 510 to 460. Another 296 ended flat.
Trading was thin ahead of Tuesday's U.S. fourth quarter Employment Cost Index. Last week, U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan expressed concern over rising wages.
Toronto's 14 sub-indices were evenly split. The strong side was led by a 1.6 percent gain in precious metals, followed by consumer products and conglomerates.
Weak groups included transportation, forestry products and financial services.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Golden Rule Resources Ltd added 0.55 to 13.10 in heavy dealings. Placer Dome Inc rose 0.80 to 28.30.
* BCE Inc, Canada's largest publicly-traded firm, slipped 0.10 to 65.65 after posting fourth quarter results that were in line with market expectations, traders said.
* Beer and entertainment firm Molson Cos rose 1.10 to 22.95. Molson announced plans to sell a 50-percent stake in retailer Reno-Deport Inc for C$62.25 million.
((Lydia Zajc, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100))
